correctness.rationale: For quotient valuation \(i\), the lifted layer has size \(|I|(q-1)q^{\ell-i-1}\), and two layers are adjacent exactly when their valuations sum to at least \(\ell\). The degree formula is strictly increasing with valuation because each new layer contributes at least two vertices while the loop-exclusion correction changes by at most one. Hence the unlabeled degree classes recover \(\ell\); consecutive class-size ratios recover \(q\); the last class gives \(|I|\). Conversely the triple fixes every layer size and every threshold adjacency. The \(\ell=2\) graph is exactly \(K_{|I|(q-1)}\), and the two stated \(K_2\) examples verify sharpness. The actual frozen verifier was read and checks symbolic profiles plus direct modular-ring graphs; those checks corroborate rather than replace the valuation proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete isomorphism classification for a canonical algebraic graph family, and the exact \(\ell=2\) collision isolates the sharp boundary where quotient and ideal parameters cease to be separately visible. The result recovers genuinely ideal-specific information, namely \(|I|\), rather than merely restating the ordinary quotient graph.
value.risk: The graph still need not determine the full ring or quotient ring isomorphism type.

final_claim: For a finite ideal-based zero-divisor graph whose quotient is a finite chain ring of nilpotency length \(\ell\ge3\), the abstract graph determines exactly \((\ell,q,|I|)\), and two such graphs are isomorphic exactly when those triples agree; at \(\ell=2\) only \(|I|(q-1)\) is recoverable.
limitations: Finite commutative rings with finite chain-ring quotient only.
No reconstruction of the full ring or ideal module structure is claimed.
